canonical_name: IKY (State Scholarships Foundation, Greece) — Foreign Nationals Scholarships
reasoning: Official iky.gr/en/foreign-citizens-scholarships-iky/ page fetched directly: IKY's foreign-nationals offerings are (1) postgraduate studies and postdoctoral research, explicitly stated as 'not open for this year', and (2) Modern Greek Language and Culture summer courses at two universities. No bachelor's/undergraduate degree scholarship for foreign students exists on this page at all. Does not meet the target ask of an undergraduate government scholarship.

Multiple scholarship-aggregator sites still list this as an active bachelor's/master's/PhD scholarship for developing-country students, but independent verification found the scheme ended in 2016 -- 'No new admissions have been possible for nearly a decade... It is not active. If you see it listed as available, the website has not been updated.' This is exactly the kind of aggregator-vs-official trap this research lane was warned about; flagging explicitly so it is not re-added by a future pass that only checks aggregator sites.

Funded by Norway's Ministry of Foreign Affairs specifically for students from Canada, Japan, Russia, South Korea, and the US. Turkey is not on this list, and no other current Norwegian government undergraduate scholarship for foreign students was found (Norway does not otherwise centrally fund non-EEA undergraduates; individual institutions may offer their own limited awards, out of scope for this 'government scholarship' lead).

Confirmed via multiple converging sources (including METU's own international cooperation office page describing the programme to its students) that Swedish Institute Scholarships -- including the track explicitly open to Turkish citizens -- are only available for full-time Master's degree programmes in Sweden. No bachelor's-level Swedish Institute scholarship exists. Turkey IS an eligible nationality for the scholarship that does exist, but the degree-level mismatch is disqualifying for this lane's undergraduate-focused ask.

Confirmed via multiple official-adjacent university sources (Danish universities' own admissions pages): 'No separate scholarship application is needed... To be considered for the scholarship you simply apply for admission to one or more of the relevant programmes... All eligible applicants who are offered study places will be automatically considered for the scholarship.' There is no distinct high-school-facing application, essay, or nomination separate from ordinary university admission -- the same 'folded into standard admission, no distinct application' pattern that caused this lane to reject Reach Oxford in Wave 1. Each Danish university also administers its own allocation independently, so there is no single canonical national programme to represent as one record.

Confirmed via multiple Finnish-university admissions sources: 'Most Finnish scholarships for bachelor's degrees are merit-based and decided at admission, so you do not need a separate competitive application -- your admission application is also your scholarship application.' The national 'Finland Scholarship' (EUR 5,000 toward year-one living costs) and individual university tuition waivers are both awarded automatically as part of ordinary admission with no distinct high-school-facing application -- the same pattern that caused this lane to reject Reach Oxford in Wave 1. There is also no single centralized government administrator (each university runs its own admission-linked award), unlike Stipendium Hungaricum or the NL Scholarship.

canonical_name: Estonian government scholarships for foreign students (BA level)
reasoning: Confirmed via the official Estonian education agency page (harno.ee): 'At the first level of higher education (BA), scholarships can be applied for only in fields related to Estonian language and culture.' Turkey IS listed among the eligible countries for Estonian degree/exchange scholarships generally, but the bachelor's-level offering is narrowly restricted to Estonian language and culture studies, not a general-purpose undergraduate scholarship usable for economics, engineering, medicine, etc. Not a good fit for this lane's target user in the vast majority of cases; separate from the Kristjan Jaak programme, which funds Estonian citizens studying abroad (the opposite direction) and is master's/PhD level only regardless.

Confirmed via the official VIAA page (viaa.gov.lv) and its own call-for-applications text: 'Applications for bachelor's... studies will be accepted from students who have successfully completed at least one academic year of studies... at the moment of application.' This means an incoming high-school graduate applying for their first year of a bachelor's degree is explicitly NOT eligible -- the scholarship is a continuation/mobility grant for students already partway through a degree, not an entry scholarship. Turkey does appear on the bilateral-agreement eligible-country list (confirmed directly on the official page, though the exact count differs between the page itself, which lists 28 countries under one agreement type, and third-party summaries citing '39' -- not resolved further since the record is rejected on the stage issue regardless), so this may be worth revisiting for a different lane covering currently-enrolled university students, but not for this high-school-facing product.

canonical_name: Lithuanian State Scholarships (ŠMPF / Education Exchanges Support Foundation)
reasoning: smpf.lrv.lt returned HTTP 403 on 2 separate WebFetch attempts (root programmes page and homepage) so this could not be confirmed first-party. Multiple independent third-party summaries converge on the same picture: Lithuania's state scholarship programme offers Lithuanian-language/culture courses, short-term (1-2 semester) study of any field, and full-time master's degree study -- but not a full bachelor's degree track. (Separately, VILNIUS TECH, one specific Lithuanian university, does run its own institutional tuition scholarship open to incoming international bachelor's students of any country -- but that is a single-university award, not a government/state programme, so it is out of scope for this specific lead even though it might be worth a different research pass.) Flagged as could_not_verify rather than a confident reject since the official state-scholarship site itself was never successfully read.

canonical_name: Icelandic Government Scholarship for Foreign Students
reasoning: The only Icelandic government scholarship found is specifically for the BA programme in 'Icelandic as a Second Language' at the University of Iceland, administered by the Árni Magnússon Institute. Eligibility explicitly requires the applicant to have ALREADY completed 1-2 years of prior university study in the humanities and to already have basic Icelandic knowledge -- doubly disqualifying for an incoming Turkish high-school graduate (wrong stage AND narrow field). No general-purpose Icelandic government undergraduate scholarship was found.

canonical_name: Turkish Coalition of America (TCA) Study Abroad Scholarships
reasoning: This programme funds the OPPOSITE direction from what this lane needs: it gives US citizens/permanent residents of specific minority heritage backgrounds (African, Armenian, Bosnian, Filipino, Hispanic/Latino, Macedonian, Native American) money to study IN Turkey, TRNC, or Bosnia and Herzegovina. It does not fund a Turkey-based Turkish student to study abroad, and applicants must already be US citizens/permanent residents enrolled at a US institution.

Official americanturkishsociety.org page confirms this fund is contingent on already having secured funding: applicants must 'demonstrate a strong interest in a STEAM field and already hold a scholarship', and the required application materials include 'Your scholarship offer letter'. This is a supplementary top-up for someone who has already secured a scholarship elsewhere, not a standalone opportunity a Turkey-based high schooler could pursue as a primary funding path. No confirmation the fund is open to Turkey-resident applicants specifically (vs. requiring an existing US scholarship/programme placement) was found either.

canonical_name: Turkish Philanthropy Funds — Changemaker Scholarship Fund
reasoning: Per official/search-indexed tpfund.org content, applicants 'must have already received partial funding from their accepted school (e.g., scholarships, grants)' before applying -- another supplementary/top-up fund rather than a standalone primary funding path, similar to the American Turkish Society's Promising Turks Fund. Distinct from the accepted Üçok Family Scholarship Fund (also administered by Turkish Philanthropy Funds), which does not require pre-secured funding and is explicitly restricted to citizens of Türkiye rather than the broader/vaguer 'of Turkish origin' framing used here.

canonical_name: Sena Eken Schieber Economics Award (Turkish Philanthropy Funds)
reasoning: Confirmed real and Turkey-connected (funds Turkish women pursuing Economics in the US), but explicitly graduate-level only: 'grants scholarships to women from Türkiye, who are admitted to graduate programs for a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Economics'. Not applicable to a high-school-bound applicant. Also gender-restricted (women only) and requires matching institutional funding.

canonical_name: Assembly of Turkish American Associations (ATAA) scholarships/youth programmes
reasoning: ATAA's only identified scholarship (with the American Association of Teachers of Turkic Languages) is graduate-student-only ($1,000, two recipients per year). Its high-school-facing offerings (UN Committee, Youth programmes) are civic-engagement/conference activities for Turkish-American youth, not scholarships, and appear oriented at diaspora students already in the US rather than general Turkey-based applicants. No standalone study-abroad funding mechanism for a Turkey-based high schooler was found.

A genuine, well-run worldwide-teen-recognition-style programme in the same family as the Diana Award, but confirmed via multiple sources to currently operate only in South Asia (Nepal, India, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh), having launched in Kathmandu in 2015. Its own stated roadmap is to expand across South Asia by 2020 and 'worldwide by 2030' -- not yet global. Türkiye is not a current or announced-next participating country.

Open to organisations and established initiatives (NGOs, social enterprises, foundations, companies, public-sector and community-based organisations) implementing an already-running, design-relevant social impact project aligned with the UN SDGs -- explicitly not for individual student concepts. Does not fit a high-school student self-application/nomination model at all.

Eligibility floor is 18, with an upper range to 35, and One Young World 'is not able to accept applications from those who will be aged under 18 at the time of the Summit' -- combined with a requirement for 'an evidenced commitment to delivering positive change' and 'a track record of generating impactful and innovative ideas', this functions as a young-professional leadership summit rather than a teen-facing recognition programme. Excludes essentially the entire 14-18 target age band for this product except the very edge of high-school graduation, at which point the track-record bar is also a high hurdle. Not a good match for the 'teen social-impact/leadership' framing of this lead.

canonical_name: UNEP Young Champions of the Earth
reasoning: Genuinely worldwide ('individuals from all countries and backgrounds are eligible') and a strong programme in general, but the age floor is a hard 18 (range 18-30), and applicants must have 'at least six months of prior experience working on their environmental project' -- both factors put this outside a realistic high-school target band. Noted here in case a future lane covering college-age/young-professional opportunities wants it; not a fit for this lane's teen-leadership-award ask.
